A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, algorithm, and synthetic study. Their main texts, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–2, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original two-dimensional optimization simulations, including regret, constraint violations, and action trajectories for PFS and comparison algorithms.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original simulation results, including comparisons averaged over 30 trials and a single-trial trajectory illustration.

M1.justification: The alternating gradient and Polyak updates remain. However, v2 revises the untightened variant's prescribed step size from Gf/(R√T) to 2R/(Gf√T), permits feasible-start tuning using an initial margin α, and defines a fallback update when the constraint subgradient is zero.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-dimensional synthetic task with quadratic losses and linear box constraints. No additional datasets, domains, or empirical test scenarios appear in the appendices.

E2.justification: Section 4 retains Yu et al. (2017)'s DPP and its tightened variant DPP-T as empirical comparators. The new discussion of Zhang et al. (2025) is an analytical comparison, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the data generation, horizon sweep from 2,000 to 20,000, evaluation metrics, and stated simulation parameters, including DPP's α=T and V=√T and DPP-T's c=20. Revised theoretical parameter prescriptions do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions include the same Figure 2 case study showing every 300th action from one trial. No ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or additional empirical analyses are introduced; the appendix additions are theoretical.

E5.justification: Both versions report Figure 1 means over 30 trials, with error bars and shading representing ±1 standard deviation. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The empirical curves and trajectories in Figures 1–2 match after accounting for rescaling and recoloring. Findings remain unchanged: PFS avoids violations, DPP has lower regret but incurs violations, and DPP-T reduces violations at increased regret. Mathematical bound changes are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 requires a nonempty level set in Assumption 4 and adds proofs connecting it to Slater's condition and permitting cost-gradient bounds only on the feasible set (Appendices C.1 and C.4). Appendix C.2 supplies the previously missing transfer of the subgradient lower bound between constraint levels. The regret proof corrects the comparator and changes Equation (7)'s R²/(2η) term to 2R²/η; several corollary constants and formulas also change. These are substantive revisions beyond theorem renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, Table 1, and conclusion retain the central claim of O(√T) regret and anytime feasibility using constraint feedback only at played actions. The delayed-feasibility and cumulative-satisfaction claims without a known feasible start also remain.

C2.justification: New Remarks 1–2 explain that boundedness plus Slater's condition suffices for the boundary-subgradient assumption, and that the feasible-start guarantee needs bounded cost gradients only on the feasible set. These clarify applicability. The interpretation of PFS's conservative trajectories and regret–feasibility tradeoff is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds an experiment-code link in Section 4 and omits v1's explicit ball-projection scaling formula. The experiment's PFS parameter reference still points to Theorem 1, although the specific feasible-start prescription has moved to Corollary 1, leaving that instruction less precise.

R1.justification: Section 1.1.3 adds Singh and Necoara (2025) and Zhang et al. (2025), distinguishing their assumptions from the online setting. New Appendix B compares update scaling and boundedness mechanisms with Zhang et al. The broader positioning against constrained and projection-free OCO remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. V2 reorganizes Section 3.2 around a general theorem and three corollaries, expands proof explanations, inserts the related-algorithm appendix, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. This is a localized structural revision rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout with running headers and revised typography. Table 1 and both figures are resized and repositioned; Figure 2 changes axis limits, ticks, and colors while retaining its trajectories. Appendices remain single-column.

improvement.justification: V2 improves theoretical support by supplying the missing boundary-subgradient argument, handling zero subgradients, and correcting several regret and step-size formulas. The new code link and related-work comparison also help. These gains are tempered by incomplete correction: Corollary 2 retains a leading regret coefficient four times smaller than substitution into the revised Theorem 1 gives, and the experiment's parameter cross-reference is stale. The net improvement is meaningful but limited.
